title: Animal Model Decision Outcomes V1
description: Shape constraints for declared per-model action losses. Unknown properties are rejected; the Rust decision kernel validates numeric/action-set invariants. Optional model_set_registry_sha256 and required_challenge_family_manifest_sha256 bind adequacy evidence to the intended scope; without those identities, qualification remains not_assessed.

model_set_registry_sha256.description: Expected digest of the exact candidate model registry being evaluated; without it, an adequacy receipt cannot qualify this decision.

required_challenge_family_manifest_sha25.description: Expected digest of the blind challenge family manifest; mismatch blocks qualification.

$comment: Schema does not check sums of model weights, equal action sets across models, valid admissible-action references, finite model values in all language bindings, or scientific adequacy. The Rust decision kernel enforces the applicable numeric/action-set invariants. If model_weight_intervals is supplied, it must name exactly the declared model set, contain each nominal model weight, and admit a simplex with total weight one; the Rust semantic kernel checks these conditions and returns worst/best expected-loss witnesses. practical_loss_difference_margin is preregistered in the same loss units as the decision objective; strict preference and practical equivalence use this margin, so near-zero numerical differences are not automatically treated as decisive. Optional adequacy-scope digests do not by themselves establish model adequacy; the separate receipt is checked by the Rust qualification gate and is still scoped evidence, not biological validation.
